*   When the two unordered CategoricalIndex objects share no common elements, the intersection must return an empty CategoricalIndex whose categories match those of the first index (not the second).

## Summary

The bug was in set operations (`union`/`intersection`) on unordered `CategoricalIndex` objects whose categories are the same set but in a different order.

**Root cause:** Two unordered categoricals with the same category set compare as equal-dtype (`CategoricalDtype.__eq__` ignores order when unordered). But a `CategoricalIndex` is backed by integer *codes* relative to its own category ordering. When both indexes are monotonic-by-codes, `union`/`intersection` take a fast path through `libjoin` (`_inner_indexer`/`_outer_indexer`), which joins on the raw codes via `_get_engine_target()`. Since the two indexes number their categories differently, the codes are not comparable — e.g. `'a'`→0 in one index and `'b'`→0 in the other — producing wrong matches. This caused an empty intersection to wrongly return an element, and union/intersection to drop or mismatch values.

**Fix:** In `pandas/core/indexes/base.py`, I applied the same guard already present in the `join` method (lines 4579-4586): right before calling `_union` and `_intersection`, when both operands are unordered `CategoricalIndex` with differing category orders, re-encode `other` to `self`'s categories:

```python
if (
    isinstance(self, ABCCategoricalIndex)
    and isinstance(other, ABCCategoricalIndex)
    and not self.ordered
    and not self.categories.equals(other.categories)
):
    other = Index(other._values.reorder_categories(self.categories), copy=False)
```

This ensures downstream code operates on comparable codes and that results use `self`'s categories (the first index), satisfying all three requirements — including the empty-intersection case returning the first index's categories.

All existing categorical and generic setop tests pass (1956 passed in the setop suites, 151 in the full categorical index suite), and I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
